findings.title: Valid commented flow keys still bypass credential scanning
findings.observation: The parser treats a source comment between apiKeys and the colon as part of the key, so normalization appends comment words and loses the sensitive suffix. The scalar assignment regex also requires whitespace directly before the colon. A one-line source-like object with this valid syntax therefore receives exit 0, SECRETS PASS and aggregate PASS.
findings.trigger: A tracked JavaScript or TypeScript object uses a comment between a plural sensitive property name and its colon.
findings.impact: A real credential can be committed while the mandatory authorization-grade checker reports PASS.

evidence.description: The tracked contract requires balanced source-like flow containers at arbitrary offsets to fail closed.
The exact-head commented-key fixture exits 0 with SECRETS PASS and no diagnostic; redacted output SHA-256 is 52ce784071c4e1cc6aef2e7766112094d337f27cd640184fafb5b0f2c609e290.

findings.remediation: Tokenize or conservatively reject supported source syntax without allowing comments or equivalent trivia to alter sensitive-key identity; add the exact commented-key composition with value-redacted diagnostics to the stock harness.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, retain deterministic positives while this exact composition and all prior structured-secret fixtures fail without emitting credential values.

findings.title: Canonical validation remains replaceable and provenance-free
findings.observation: Production discovery searches HOME, account home and CODEX_HOME plugin caches, then selects the lexically last full path without proving current package identity. The selected module is executed and its version or digest is absent from authority observations. A permissive CODEX_HOME-local candidate makes an empty-plan state rejected by the installed workflowctl receive 13/13 PASS.
findings.trigger: Multiple validator candidates exist across supported roots, or CODEX_HOME contains another lifecycle package cache.
findings.impact: Workflowctl-invalid durable state can still authorize PASS, validator choice varies by filesystem layout, and two different validators can produce the same authority digest.

evidence.description: The tracked contract requires the current installed workflowctl validator and deterministic canonical authority.

Installed workflowctl rejects the empty plan while the unmodified checker selects the CODEX_HOME candidate and returns 13/13 PASS; output SHA-256 is 987890c9306a1f6f65a9d6146ae7de0af94a7b99e1898e19323906f9628df76a.
Independent source inspection confirms lexical full-path selection and missing validator provenance in authority observations.

findings.remediation: Resolve exactly one validator from trusted active lifecycle-package metadata, reject ambiguous or unsupported candidates, and bind a path-independent validator version plus content digest into authority observations and deterministic output.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, the production resolver must reject extra-root and multi-version ambiguity, installed workflowctl rejection must always imply checker rejection, and changing validator identity must change or invalidate authority evidence.

findings.title: Repository-wide allowlist rejects future implementation heads
findings.observation: The production checker compares every git-tracked path with a fixed list of the current management documents and sources. The lifecycle harness deletes its temporary implementation files before committing the advertised implementation head. Retaining one ordinary source artifact makes FILES fail even though the public contract requires later IP implementation, review, merge and synchronized management updates.
findings.trigger: Any independent IP adds a normal tracked source, test, migration, workflow or deployment file before the management projection is validated.
findings.impact: The checker can validate only the documentation snapshot and cannot validate the future In Progress, In Review, Accepted or reopened states it claims to support.

evidence.description: Requirements require each IP to implement, verify, prepare an independent PR and synchronize management state.
Adding one ordinary future source artifact makes only FILES fail as unexpected; output SHA-256 is bbf1ce9fc4d886cf356f20af1598868d12bc4b9a904fdd7ebfcdcacf5be49504.
Independent inspection confirms fixed repository-wide equality and that the stock lifecycle matrix removes temporary implementation files before its implementation head.

findings.remediation: Require the managed documents and exact eight-file plan-directory set without equating the entire repository tracked-file set to the current snapshot; preserve parallel-ledger and generated-artifact defenses and add a positive lifecycle case retaining normal implementation and test files.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, a workflowctl-generated non-Draft lifecycle fixture with retained source/test files must pass while extra plan files, alternate ledgers and generated artifacts still fail.

Neither source names the later cycle-four PASS snapshot.

findings.impact: The public project entry rewrites rather than faithfully projects upstream authority, making the current approval state internally contradictory and unauditable from the linked documents.

findings.verification: At a new exact head, the Current portfolio, linked source headers and immutable cycle-four PASS proof must agree on phase, decision, commit and authority.
